notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (customer engagement/chat automation). Starting Hosted API eval focused on streaming + function/tool calling. Long-term interest in Dedicated if SLA/throughput predictable and pricing fits. Priority: regional latency (NA/EU) and smart routing/fallbacks for uptime.

Timeline / recent activities:
- 2026-02-10: Intro call (AE Priya) — product fit OK, provided quickstart and security FAQ.
- 2026-02-15: Hosted API walkthrough (demo) — showed streaming + tool-calling pattern (search + order-lookup). CTO Rajesh: "EU users complain about lag; need <300ms p95 for interactive flows."
- 2026-02-18: Deep dive with SE (Liam) — discussed batching, KV cache for session continuity, and model variants for fallback. Fireflies id ff-20260218-VC.
- 2026-02-22: POC kickoff — SE to run perf harness from NA & EU vantage points; sample workloads: 1) customer support chat (avg 120 tokens), 2) automation agents invoking internal tools.
- 2026-02-26: Demo round 2 — streaming latency observed ~p95 420ms from EU region to hosted endpoint; acceptable for some flows but below Vera's target. Fireflies id ff-20260226-demo.
- 2026-03-04: Security questionnaire submitted (drive:/security/vera-chatworks/sec-answers-2026-02). Legal requests data residency language for EU traffic.

POC details / technical asks (from SE/CTO):
- Workload: real-time chat/assistant that must stream tokens to web clients and perform tool-calls (search, ticket lookup, order status).
- SLOs: target p95 end-to-end component latency <300-400ms for interactive flows; throughput target 40-60 reqs/sec for peak; concurrency ~150 simultaneous sessions.
- Regional routing: want NA/EU edge routing with EU residency for EU-labeled accounts. Must support routing policy + automatic fallback to compatible model variant when primary region saturated.
- Streaming: chunked responses for progressive rendering; want stable first-byte latency budget for perceived interactivity.
- Fallbacks: policy options discussed — fall back to smaller cheaper model or cached reply, OR route to alternate region if acceptable by residency rules. They prefer routing-based fallback vs blind model-swapping.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, trace for function calls.

Commercial / pricing notes:
- Starting evaluation on Hosted API; if POC shows consistent latency + cost predictability, they will consider Dedicated reserved capacity for critical flows.
- Price sensitivity: moderate — conservative on unit cost but willing to pay for stable SLOs and predictable billing. ARR expectation for first year ~$100k-$250k.

Quotes / disposition snippets:
- CTO Rajesh: "If EU users still feel lag, adoption stalls. We need clear routing + fallback playbook."
- Head of Product Maya: "Tool-calls are non-negotiable — we must keep structured tool outputs and retries idempotent."

Open items / next steps:
- SE (Liam) to run perf harness from AWS eu-west & us-east zones and deliver 95/99 latencies by 2026-03-10. Include token-cost per-session estimate.
- AE (Priya) to share Dedicated pricing ranges and reserve-capacity options by 2026-03-09.
- Legal to review proposed data-residency clause; Vera to confirm whether routing EU->NA is allowed for non-EU accounts.
- Decision criteria: pass latency SLO in EU for 3 continuous days OR acceptance of fallback routing with documented user impact.
